title: Domestication of cotton
summary: Four cotton species were domesticated independently by four different civilizations, each several thousand years ago: two native to Africa and Arabia, and two in the Americas, first in the Yucatan and northwest South America. The oldest known cotton in the Indian subcontinent is thread preserved in a copper bead from a Neolithic burial at Mehrgarh, of the sixth millennium BCE, though it may not be from a domesticated plant. Cotton is now the world's most widely used plant textile.
